newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kone warning fuels more analysts' doubts.
newsitem.headline: Kone warning fuels more analysts' doubts.

text.p: Finnish share analysts said on Thursday they would lower their earnings forecasts for Kone after the group warned its full-year 1996 earnings would be close to zero.
Vesa Sahivirta, analyst at Postipankki said he would lower profit forecasts for 1996, 1997 and 1998 for Kone.
"I already had a very pessimistic view on the company, but now I have to cut my forecasts further," Sahivirta told Reuters.

Kone announced that group full-year 1996 earnings after tax were expected to be "close to zero". Full-year 1996 losses on its Italian operations would rise to almost 200 million markka. Kone had earlier targetted a bigger 1996 profit than in 1995.
Kone also said it expected 1997 earnings to "improve only slightly" from the current year. The 1998 result was expected to be substantially better, the company said.
Sahivirta said he will keep his sell/underweight recommendation for Kone. @
"I think the stock is expensive compared to projected earnings," he said. Kone had at that stage shed 35.00 markka to 500.00 markka.
Merita Securities analyst Jari Koskela said he would lower his profit forecasts for Kone for 1996 and 1997.
"I have to do a more detailed study of (Kone's) 1998 prospects to be able to decide whether I have to change my recommendation for the stock," Koskela said.
"We have been cautious on Kone," he added, but declined to give his recommendation.

Opstock analyst Jukka Linden also said he would lower 1996 and 1997 earnings forecasts for Kone. He could not yet say whether Opstock would keep its underweight recommendation for the stock as it had fallen significantly since the release of the profit-warning.
At 1645/1345 GMT, Kone traded at 488.00 markka, down 47.00 markka or 8.8 percent.
